analysis: Treponema pallidum is the causative agent of syphilis, and the standard treatment for this infection is Penicillin G. This antibiotic is highly effective against Treponema pallidum and is considered the first-line treatment. While alternatives like Tetracycline, Azithromycin, and Doxycycline can be used, they are not the preferred options. Tetracycline and Doxycycline are effective but are generally reserved for patients who are allergic to penicillin or in specific cases. Azithromycin is also used in penicillin-allergic patients but is not the first-line treatment. Therefore, based on established medical guidelines and consensus, Penicillin G is the drug of choice for treating Treponema pallidum infections.
